title: EFS & FSx File Storage
summary: Shared file systems for Linux, Windows, HPC and multiprotocol workloads.
services: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
tldr: **EFS**: managed NFS for Linux, elastic capacity, shared by EC2, ECS/Fargate, EKS and Lambda across AZs. Regional EFS survives an AZ loss.
**FSx for Windows File Server**: SMB with Active Directory and Windows ACLs. **FSx for Lustre**: HPC/ML scratch or persistent file system linked to S3.
**FSx for NetApp ONTAP**: NFS *and* SMB (and iSCSI) on the same data, snapshots, SnapMirror, dedup, tiering. **FSx for OpenZFS**: ZFS snapshots and clones over NFS.
Spiky, unpredictable EFS throughput → **Elastic Throughput**; rarely read files → lifecycle to **EFS IA** and **EFS Archive**.

keyFacts.text: **Elastic Throughput** scales up and down with the workload and bills per use. **Bursting** ties throughput to stored size, so small file systems run out of credits.
EFS **Standard**, **Infrequent Access** and **Archive**. Lifecycle policies move files by last access and can move them back on first access.
**FSx for Lustre scratch** keeps no replicated copy and is cheapest for short jobs whose source data lives in S3. **Persistent** replicates data within its AZ for long-running work.
FSx for Windows, ONTAP and OpenZFS offer **Multi-AZ** deployments with automatic failover. EFS One Zone and FSx Single-AZ do not survive an AZ loss.
**EFS replication** keeps a read-only copy in another Region or AZ with a 15-minute RPO for most file systems.

traps: EFS is NFS for Linux. Windows instances needing SMB and AD want FSx for Windows File Server.
FSx for Windows File Server speaks SMB only. Linux NFS and Windows SMB clients on the same data need ONTAP.
Adding dummy files to earn EFS burst credits is a hack; the answer is Elastic Throughput.
Provisioned Throughput sized for the peak pays for that peak 24/7. Choose Elastic for unpredictable spikes.
FSx for Lustre is not the answer for Windows or general office shares; it's for compute-heavy Linux workloads.
Two Single-AZ FSx file systems synced with DFS Replication is more work than one Multi-AZ file system.
